items.title: Peer Support and Supervisor Boundaries
items.description: Maintaining professional boundaries can be challenging, especially when working in supportive services, such as peer recovery or recovery housing. This course begins the conversation and offers tools to help you with confidentiality, boundary setting, guidelines for self-disclosure, and organizational climates to help identify, establish, and maintain healthy boundaries in professional support work. Course Objectives: Identify Confidentiality & HIPAA compliance; Define boundaries and their benefits; Discuss Guidelines for Self Disclosure; Discuss organizational co-worker boundaries.

items.title: Part 2: Levels of Recovery Residences - CORR
Part 1: Intro to Recovery Residences - CORR
Confidentiality and Ethics: Webinar
items.description: Fear of stigma is a primary reason why individuals do not seek treatment. Your recovery home residents, in particular, may fear what others think and how a loss of confidentiality might affect their potential employment. Dr. Kenneth Martz presents "Confidentiality, Ethics, and Substance Abuse Treatment," which explores confidentiality laws, how to work within them, and issues of particular interest to recovery homeowners and operators, all in the context of what Dr. Martz calls "the intricate dance between confidentiality and community in the pursuit of recovery."

items.title: Cultural Humility in a Recovery Environment
items.description: Recognizing and practicing of cultural humility can transform your recovery house. The course examines how your emotional and cultural intelligence serves the development of cultural humility.

items.title: The Role of Recovery Allies: Webinar
items.description: Alison Webb is a recovery coach, public health specialist, and certified prevention specialist who's worked over 15 years in the field of substance use prevention, treatment, and recovery. In this course she addresses the age-old question of What Can I Do?  No matter who's asking - friend, family, neighbor, or community member - it's good to have an answer that will stand the test of time. Alison discusses how you can serve as an ally to support recovery, recovery housing, and other supportive services that build recovery capital. As Alison says, “Most adults with substance use disorder don’t receive specialized treatment like counseling, medication, or rehab. Instead, the recovery journey starts in their communities, among family and friends, here and now, with their recovery allies."

items.title: Understanding and Responding to NIMBYISM in Communities
items.description: NIMBY (Not In My Back Yard) is a characterization of opposition by residents in a rural or urban community, to proposed developments in their local area. These developments could include the location of new recovery housing.  This course can assist you with recognizing and navigating situations where NIMBY occurs.

items.title: Recovery House Management: Creating a Supportive Internal Community
items.description: When a recovery residence employs the Peer-led, Peer-Driven Social Model, it provides its residents with an environment designed to empower them to make decisions, to be part of a recovery community, to be comfortable and safe, and to learn and grow.

items.title: First Aid for Common Household Injuries
items.description: This course will provide recovery house operators, staff, and clients with the base knowledge to respond to minor common household injuries that may occur.

items.title: Integrated Recovery Residences and Supports into the ASAM Criteria
items.description: Welcome to the Fletcher Group's course on how the American Society of Addiction Medicine (ASAM) has, for the first time, integrated recovery services like mutual-support and peer support groups, recovery housing , and employment training into comprehensive treatment planning. The Learning Objectives for this course are: Introduce the important changes about recovery supports and recovery residences in ASAM: Provide information about the evidence and conceptual frameworks used to fully integrated recovery support services into ASAM treatment planning, and; Learn about ASAM’s recommended assessment tools in recovery capital.

items.title: Pregnant and Parenting Complexities in Recovery Housing
items.description: In this course, we will briefly touch on the prevalence of pregnant individuals with a substance use disorder; housing considerations for individuals that are pregnant, postpartum, and or parenting; recovery house partnerships; early recovery and parenting; medication to support recovery; infant withdrawal, needs, and other considerations; and provide a few national resources for deeper education and support.

items.title: Naloxone Training by PAR
items.description: Everyone should know how to properly administer Naloxone medication, how it works, and where to access the medication. This course provides the basic tools to educate you in these areas.

items.title: CPR: Hands Only
items.description: This is a high level course designed to support recovery house operators, staff, and clients to understand how to respond to minor injuries that may occur in the home.

items.title: Certification Standards for Colorado Recovery Housing
items.description: Based on the recovery housing standards designed by the National Alliance of Recovery Residences, this course introduces the Colorado Recovery Residences 2025 Standards guidebook and best practices.

items.title: How Physical & Social Activity Aids Recovery: Webinar
items.description: "When a diverse group of individuals pulls together, inspiring things happen." That's the idea behind The Phoenix, a non-profit founded in 2006 that encourages physical and social activity as a means of generating the sense of connection, self-efficacy, and resilience people need to recover from substance use. In this course, the Senior Manager of Research and Evaluation Beth Collinson and National Partnerships Manager Chelsea Dueitt Burge discuss the unique approach that has gained The Phoenix nearly 200,000 members in 44 different states. This is an inspiring lesson in how commitment, action and connection can turn lives around.

items.title: Clarifying Language and Acronyms: Substance Use Disorders and Medications
items.description: Acronyms can create confusion, especially when there are many acronyms surrounding a particular topic. Key terms in recovery and treatmenet are no exception. This overview emphasizes the importance of clear language in addressing these complex issues.

items.title: An Introduction to NARR Levels of Recovery Housing
items.description: The National Alliance for Recovery Residences (NARR) defines four levels of recovery housing, with each providing varying levels of support and structure. These levels are not a rigid step-down continuum, but rather they meet the needs of individuals as they move through their recovery journey and support them as their circumstances change. This course provides an overview of the levels to help new owners and operators decide the support they wish to provide to residents. Upon completion of this course, learners will be able to: Define each Level of Recovery Residences; Recognize the primary differences between the Levels of Recovery Residences; Identify the Level for their new or existing recovery residence.

items.title: How a Recovery Residence Inspection Works
items.description: Recovery residences in Colorado that are certified, or wish to be, will undergo a physical inspection of the property. The inspection assesses the overall safety, quality, and condition of the residence and ensures it meets the standards established for Colorado. The inspection process includes a physical inspection of the premises, a review of required documentation, and resident interviews. This course covers the physical inspection and demonstrates how to accurately prepare for and participate in a site inspection by connecting CO state standards to the inspection process and appropriate recovery residence levels. Learner Outcomes: Describe the Colorado site inspection process: Apply the information to prepare your recovery residence for a Colorado certification inspection(s)

items.title: Understanding the Colorado Recovery Housing Grievance Process & FAQs
items.description: The Colorado Recovery Residences complaint/grievance policy ensures a clear and transparent process for handling Complaints or Grievances submitted to CARR and that handling those grievances respectfully, appropriately, and professionally. The Formal Complaint/Grievance Procedure should be used: To resolve complaints by individuals or entities against certified recovery residence providers and their staff, owners, and operators. To provide the public with clearer information and directions for accessing this process, promote transparency, and improve user experience. To serve as a mechanism to report issues with existing CARR policy that certified recovery residences, stakeholders, and other state agencies believe should be examined prior to the next scheduled annual policy review meeting.  Grievance Process FAQs: Got questions about the CARR Grievance Process? We have answers! This brief course provides the answers to the most frequently asked questions CARR receives regarding the recovery residence Grievance Process.

items.title: Understanding HIPAA and 42 CFR Part 2 in Recovery Residences
items.description: Breaches of confidentiality in a recovery residence can lead to stress, anxiety, and a sense of betrayal, which may trigger a return to use. Maintaining confidentiality helps create a supportive and secure environment conducive to long-term recovery. Protecting confidentiality ensures a safe, supportive, and legally compliant environment where individuals can focus on their recovery without fear of exposure or judgment. Learning Objectives: Be introduced to HIPAA and 42 CFR Part 2 and the possible applicability of these two federal laws to recovery residences; Understand the importance of HIPAA and 42 CFR Part 2 and their impact on confidentiality in recovery housing

items.title: Intermediate Evaluation
items.description: This course will provide students with a detailed overview of evaluation instruments and tools. This course will consist of five modules covering resident outcomes of interest, construction and use of a data shell, simple data analysis, data visualization, and reporting. A basic knowledge of Excel is expected, but not required.  The course helps recovery house owners, operators, and managers.

items.title: Insurance and Budgeting for Recovery Housing
items.description: Purchasing insurance for your recovery house is different from what you would purchase for your own home. Recovery housing insurance is nuanced and may require discussions with your board and insurance agent. And not all insurance agents are skilled in recovery housing insurance. You may have to look at other insurance companies to get appropriate coverage. This course provides you with an overview of the different items you should investigate as you begin shopping for insurance for the house.- Budgeting for Recovery Housing: When developing a recovery house, it is important to identify ways to sustain your operation. This course covers the basics of recovery house financing considerations, including capital expenses, operating expenses, stopgap funding, and ways to become sustainable.

items.title: Foundations of Self Care - CRH (how to practice - be hear now - meditation basics - 988
items.description: These microlearning courses cover some basic self care practices including meditation and some simple yoga practices to calm and center ones self. Sometimes, we need more help than we can give ourselves, so we also provide an overview of the SAMHSA 988 Crisis Line and its resources. How to Practice Self Care - This course provides an overview of self-care and why it is important for everyone, particularly those in recovery. Be Here Now - Yoga/Meditation for Self Care - Yoga is a great wellness tool for self-care and can help those in recovery develop breathing skills to refocus and calm. Meditation Basics: Mindfulness and Loving-Kindness Meditation - Meditation is a relaxation technique that can help reduce stress and calm our minds. This course covers two types of meditation that may benefit those in recovery: Mindfulness Meditation and Loving-Kindness Meditation. SAMHSA 988 Crisis Line - The course will help learners to understand what the 988 Crisis Lifeline is, how it works, and identify best practices for sharing information about the 988 Crisis Lifeline and other resources.

items.title: Implementing Medication Assisted Recovery
items.description: In this course, we'll cover changes in the illicit drug supply and how these changes are impacting trends in overdoses and deaths. We'll discuss how to create a plan to support safe use of life-saving addiction medications in recovery homes, minimizing the risk of diversion. We also outline strategies to help you evaluate options for working with different kinds of healthcare providers that can work with you to streamline your residents' access to addiction treatment medications. We'll introduce a resource you can use to evaluate your best options in providing mutual support curricula and peer support groups that don't stigmatize medications for addiction. We'll help you to create policies and procedures to safely and manage FDA-approved addiction medications on-site, with special attention to the Department of Justice guidance on the Americans with Disabilities Act that assures access to medications for treating opioid use disorder. Finally, we'll review compliance concerns with this act and the Fair Housing Act, sharing case scenarios and additional information.

items.title: Preventing Medication Assisted Recovery (MAR) Related Discrimination
items.description: This training will provide information on Discrimination Policies for Recovery Housing operators. After completion, the participant will have the knowledge to confidently operate a non-discriminatory recovery house.

items.title: Job Interview Best Practices
items.description:
Marshall Health's Creating Opportunities for Recovery Employment proudly presents our series on employability. 

In this module, you'll discover best practices for job interviews. 

First, you'll develop your Interview Day Checklist. Checklists reduce a lot of the stress and help you to focus on the interview itself. 

Blueprint for Nailing Your Interview outlines the five steps you can take to build your own Blueprint for Nailing Your Interview.

items.title: Build Your Resume and Apply for Jobs
items.description: Marshall Health's Creating Opportunities for Recovery Employment proudly presents our series on employability. Building Your Resume: Building a great resume is made easy by following the best practices outlined in this course. Applying for a Job:  Don't get stressed out over the prospect of applying for a job. Following the best practices outlined in this course makes applying for a job easy and (mostly) stressfree!

items.title: Preparing for Your Job Search
items.description: Marshall Health's Creating Opportunities for Recovery Employment proudly presents our series on employability. The more you know about your personality, unique qualities, abilities, and values, the better you will be able to identify the right career path. Get to Know You outlines how you can take a deeper dive into learning what makes you uniquely you. Exploring Career Goals is all about discovering educational, training, and professional opportunities that complement your interests, passion, and goals. Defining your interests and skills helps you to determine career interests, which in turn can put you on the right path to bring your career aspirations to reality.

items.title: Addiction as a Chronic Disease: Webinar
items.description: In keeping with his belief that "choice versus disease" is a false dichotomy, Dr. Alex Elswick makes his case for a more humane, sensible, and effective approach to addiction. In addition to explaining why an SUD should be thought of as a chronic disorder, Dr. Elswick addresses the importance of reducing stigma, the most salient risk factors for substance use, and the community-based policies, practices, and resources needed to support people in recovery. Dr. Elswick's multi-faceted knowledge and experience has been shared with numerous local, state, and federal agencies with the goal of creating legislation that supports recovery. But it is his own life experience as a person in long-term recovery that has convinced him that the traditional acute treatment model is misguided. "For me, addiction was suffering, plain and simple," says Dr. Elswick. "But what really helped me finally find sustained recovery was the  complete continuum of care that stretched from six months of inpatient to six weeks of intensive outpatient to years of therapy with no gaps in care. That kind of chronic disease management ensured that I was never unsupported and never alone. I had access to so much recovery capital, including stable housing, meaningful employment with benefits, and transportation." It's that experience, says Dr. Elswick, that has led him to believe that "people recover when their needs are met.”

items.title: Recovery Ecosystems for Communities
items.description: Recovery Ecosystems are paramount to removing barriers to success for people with Substance Use Disorder (SUD), especially for those living in rural communities.

items.title: Urine Analysis (UA) Best Practices - CORR (2 resident and urine)
items.description: Recovery homes may use urine analysis for their residents centered on supporting each person's recovery journey. According to the National Institutes of Health (NIH), urine testing is the best developed and most commonly used monitoring technique in recovery programs. Understanding Urine Analysis - Urine analysis is the best-developed and most-used monitoring technique in substance use treatment programs across the continuum of care. When used correctly and competently following best practice guidelines, it can be an effective therapeutic tool. Drug testing uses a biological sample to detect the presence or absence of a specific drug (or drugs) and drug metabolites within a specific window of time. No universal standard exists today in clinical drug testing for addiction identification, diagnosis, treatment, medication monitoring, or recovery. Urine Analysis: From a Resident Perspective - This course will explain urine analysis from the residents perspective. Providing person-first care, dignity, and respect is hugely important to your residents. This course explains how urine analysis can affect the resident.

items.title: Peer Leadership Best Practices  (2 - rr how we know they work & so you want to be a peer leader)
items.description: So You Want to Become a Peer Leader in a Recovery Residence? Recovery residence house managers and others wishing to become “peer leaders” (PL) will be able to listen to interviews of six successful PLs and hear how they approached the role, the challenges they faced, and what their experiences have taught them. Anyone interested in learning more about this process of becoming a PL and their vital role in recovery residence operations will enjoy this program. At the conclusion of this program, participants will understand the knowledge, skills, and abilities needed to function in the role, as well as the challenges and opportunities involved. Recovery Residences - How We Know They Work Many in the recovery field feel intuitively that recovery residences, structured sober living, and similar programs aid a person’s recovery from Substance Use Disorder (SUD). Unfortunately, there has been scant research to measure outcomes and explore the questions around recovery residences: What evidence do we have that supports our ideas that recovery housing helps recovery? What types of programs have the most success? The least? What does the data tell us that may help develop evidence-based programs?  Dr. Corey Vilsaint, a community research psychologist fellow at Harvard Medical School and Massachusetts General Hospital, and a principal investigator at the Recovery Research Institute and Center for Addiction Medicine, answers these questions and more in this course.

items.title: Recovery House Supervision Best Practices
items.description: This module covers two primary aspects of supervising recovery housing - the community INSIDE of the house and the community OUTSIDE of the house. Recovery House Management - Creating a Supportive Internal Community & Recovery House Management - Understanding & Responding to NIMBYism in Communities.

items.title: Managing Staff
items.description: This series covers 3 major pieces of effective staff management:  Communication, Listening, and Delegation.  Explore ways to improve your management skills and create successful teams.

items.title: SWOT Analysis
items.description: SWOT Analysis is a strategic tool organizations use to identify their strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, and 'threats.' The tool is a way to help a rural recovery house board agree on what they do best now and develop strategies for the future. This course covers the basics of SWOT Analysis and the basics of using the tool.

items.title: Colorado Recovery Housing Code of Ethics
items.description: Colorado requires certified recovery houses to maintain and uphold the highest standards of ethical conduct. This course shares each of Colorado’s Code of Ethics to help you recognize the complex ethical challenges in recovery housing and reflects Colorado’s commitment to excellence and integrity. Learning Objectives: Learners will understand the Code of Ethics as outlined by Colorado

items.title: A Guide to Individualized Recovery Planning
items.description: Recovery support is a crucial component of the continuum and quality care. Effective recovery staff enhances community culture, improves program outcomes, and implements best practices in recovery residences; allowing your program to operate efficiently and with less incidences. This course will equip you with a comprehensive understanding and the necessary skills for substance use disorder, recovery support, and supportive care. Learning Objectives: Learners will assess the recovery house culture and their role within that culture; Learners will be able to integrate individual resident culture into the recovery house culture to respect the individual and improve overall outcomes.

items.title: Why Evaluation Matters in Recovery Residences
items.description: This course shows the importance of collecting data for a recovery house and how it can improve your house operations. Find out why evaluation matters, what data is the most valuable to collect, and how to evaluate and use the data you secure. Learning Objective: Learners will be able to identify components of evaluation.

items.title: Good Neighbor and Community Engagement
items.description: Recovery residences play a crucial role in supporting individuals with substance use disorders within community settings. However, the stigma associated with substance use disorder and the unique challenges of operating these residences can create significant hurdles. The Good Neighbor and Community Engagement course is designed to equip owners and operators of recovery residences with the knowledge and skills needed to successfully manage these programs within neighborhoods and communities. By combining best practices from industry leaders, this course provides practical strategies to navigate these complexities and enhance the effectiveness of recovery residences. Learning Objectives: Create a good neighbor policy; Implement guidelines and expectations to foster relationships between recovery residences and the local community; Relieve stress from operators around community engagement

items.title: Resident Rights & Responsibilities
items.description: This course is for owners and operators of recovery residences, to ensure you are fully informed of resident rights and responsibilities. We aim to create a safe, supportive, and transparent environment that fosters sustainable recovery and protects individual's rights.  The course outlines the key rights of residents, including understanding the recovery residence's priority population and goals, financial terms and obligations, reporting concerns without fear of retaliation, and access to personal and financial information. Additionally, it guarantees residents fair housing rights and addresses policies regarding personal property. Learning Objectives: Create a resident rights policy; Define what is and is not a resident right

items.title: Imposter Syndrome: What It Is and How to Overcome It
items.description:
Do you ever get a nagging feeling that you’re a fraud? A feeling like you don’t deserve your accomplishments, you’ll never be “good enough,” and it’s only a matter of time before people find out? That feeling, while isolating, is common. And it has a name: impostor syndrome.

Impostor syndrome is a type of chronic self-doubt that causes us to feel like we’re inadequate, despite evidence showing otherwise. The result is that we become our own worst enemy—selling ourselves short and hurting our workplace performance. So, what does it take to overcome impostor syndrome?

In this course, you’ll learn to define impostor syndrome and determine whether it’s something you’re experiencing. Then, you’ll learn how impostor syndrome holds you back as well as six strategies to face your insecurities head-on.

items.description: The course will help learners to understand what the 988 Crisis Lifeline is, how it works, and identify best practices for sharing information about the 988 Crisis Lifeline and other resources.
